A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 31-page versions of the same work. Their main sections, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–D can be reliably matched despite the added figure and resulting reflow.

before.justification: v2 reports original quadratic optimization experiments, GPT-2 training on OpenWebText, ResNet18 training on CIFAR-10, and empirical Hessian measurements in Section 4, Figures 1–3 and Tables 1–4.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experimental results and additionally displays optimizer trajectories on original and rotated quadratic functions in Figure 2.

M1.justification: The Adam, AdaSGD, blockwise Adam and Hessian-norm estimation procedures in Algorithms 1–4 are unchanged. The new trajectory illustration introduces no algorithmic component or update-rule revision.

E1.justification: Both versions cover quadratic optimization, GPT-2 language modeling on OpenWebText, and ResNet18 classification on CIFAR-10. Figure 2 adds a small example within the existing quadratic rotation setting, without expanding task or domain coverage.

E2.justification: The added quadratic trajectory comparison includes SGD alongside AdaSGD, Adam and SignGD. v2's quadratic Table 1 compared AdaSGD and Adam variants without SGD. SignGD was already represented there by Adam with both beta parameters zero, so its explicit naming is not an entirely new comparator.

E3.justification: Figure 2 adds a two-dimensional trajectory comparison before and after rotation alongside the retained 1,000-dimensional, 100-step quadratic evaluation. Its exact objective and optimizer settings are not specified. The existing Section 4 training budgets, learning-rate searches, preprocessing and metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds a visual case study examining how coordinate rotation affects optimizer trajectories, with paired contour plots and marked starting points. The existing rotation experiments, learning-rate sensitivity analysis and batch-size comparisons are retained.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains the same ten-seed evaluation and mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting. No run counts, uncertainty estimation procedures, confidence intervals or statistical tests are added or revised; the new trajectory figure adds no uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: New Figure 2 supplies trajectory results illustrating preserved path shapes under rotation for SGD and AdaSGD, and altered paths for Adam and SignGD. Tables 1–4 and all previously reported GPT-2 and CIFAR-10 curves retain their results; this is additional illustrative evidence, not a same-setting performance improvement.

T1.justification: The equivariance theorem, smoothness definitions, convergence results, Hessian-estimation guarantee and proofs in Appendices A–D are substantively unchanged. Figure 2 illustrates the existing Theorem 2.2. The added punctuation in the proof of Lemma 3.13 does not change its mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, four introductory contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about rotation-dependent geometry, Adam's convergence, blockwise generalization and empirical smoothness measurements. The new illustration supports an existing claim without changing its scope.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning geometry, convergence speed and learning-rate stability, together with the limitation concerning momentum theory, are retained. The new caption restates the established equivariance distinction, and the Adam–SignGD similarity was already discussed in the introduction.

D1.justification: The code-access information, experimental settings and Appendix D implementation details are unchanged, including RandPerm rotations and the 200/50 Cauchy-vector counts for GPT-2/ResNet18 Hessian estimation. No corresponding implementation recipe is added for the new trajectory illustration.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive comparisons with prior research are unchanged. Differences in bibliography backreferences reflect shifted page locations rather than added references or revised positioning.

P1.justification: Section 2 gains a brief introduction to the new visual example and its explanatory caption. Crossreferences and minor punctuation are updated, while section order and nearly all existing prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 adds the two-panel Figure 2 with a side caption. Former Figures 2–3 become Figures 3–4, Algorithm 3 and Table 2 shift placement, and surrounding pages reflow. Existing plots and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: Figure 2 makes the central rotation-equivariance distinction easier to understand by showing optimizer paths before and after rotation alongside Theorem 2.2. The existing theory and quantitative evidence are preserved. This is a limited explanatory improvement; the illustration's unspecified settings limit its additional empirical value.
